creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Evidence for a_2LMQSW9A8 and a_2LO4kETFT, kept separate so the fix cards stay about the fix.

Every slot in a four-agent parallel round lost time to the same two bugs, and three of the four first mistook them for something they had broken.

    round 1  slot 3  reported pane_equipping failing at 96e0573 with zero Rust changes
    round 2  slot 1  root-caused it after 30-run and 20-run measurement samples
    round 2  slot 2  chased Declined("timed out") in daemon_settings as its own corpus bug
    round 2  slot 4  spent two full gate runs chasing pane_equipping and split_sides
    round 2  integrator  reported a red gate as green, then had to correct it

`split_sides` is a sixth known member, found by slot 4. It and `pane_equipping` each failed one of two full runs at load 80-106, a different one each run, and **both pass alone in under 5 seconds** - independent support for slot 1 measurement that the waits are nowhere near their 20s allowance.

## Why the cost is out of proportion to the bug

The failure does not name its cause. It surfaces as a timeout in whichever daemon-backed test loses the run, so it reads as a flake in the work the reader is holding. Each agent had to re-derive that it was not theirs, and one of them was wrong about it for a while.

That is the pattern worth taking from this rather than the individual bugs: a defect that points at the wrong culprit costs far more than the failures it causes. Two other cards from the same round have the same shape - a_2LOHfLmsL reports a delivered write as a refusal, and a_2LONhlgwh fails at publickey rather than saying whose key the container holds.

Worth asking of any error path: does this failure name its real cause, or does it hand the reader somebody else fault to investigate?
title: What the flake family cost four agents in two rounds
